claims.claim: A $40 million LOTTO MAX ticket sold in Grey County was validated at an OLG terminal hours before a midnight deadline.
claims.episode_span: validated at an OLG lottery terminal with just hours left before a midnight deadline
claims.source_title: $40M Lotto ticket sold in Grey County claimed hours before expiry
claims.supporting_quote: According to the OLG, the ticket was validated at an OLG lottery terminal, with just hours before the midnight deadline.

claims.claim: The ticket was sold for the October 28, 2025 LOTTO MAX draw.
claims.episode_span: the ticket was sold for the October 28, 2025 draw
claims.source_title: $40M Lotto ticket sold in Grey County claimed hours before expiry
claims.supporting_quote: The ticket was sold for the October 28, 2025 LOTTO MAX draw.

claims.claim: OLG contacted the people who validated the ticket and will meet them to determine rightful ownership.
claims.episode_span: OLG said it has contacted the person or persons who validated the ticket
claims.source_title: $40M Lotto ticket sold in Grey County claimed hours before expiry
claims.supporting_quote: OLG has made contact with the person(s) that validated the ticket. The next step is for OLG to meet with the person(s) in order to determine if they are the rightful owner(s) of the ticket

claims.claim: If unclaimed by the end of October 28, the $40 million prize would have returned to the Lotto Max pool and ranked as Canada's second-largest unclaimed Lotto Max prize, behind a $70 million Scarborough ticket from June 28, 2022.
claims.episode_span: would have been Canada's second-largest unclaimed Lotto Max prize, behind a $70 million ticket
claims.source_title: $40M Grey County lotto ticket could become Canada's second largest unclaimed prize
claims.supporting_quote: It would also become Canada's second largest unclaimed Lotto Max prize, behind a $70 million winning ticket from the June 28, 2022 draw. That unclaimed ticket was sold in Scarborough, Ontario.

claims.claim: Bayshore Broadcasting listed Yvonne Hamlin as Collingwood mayor, Chris Potts as deputy mayor, and Christopher Baines, Marianne Mcleod, Rob Ring, Ian MacCulloch, Jan Ferrigan, James McCrimmon and Steve Perry as councillors.

claims.claim: Marni Moreau won The Blue Mountains mayor's race with 2,469 votes (41.1 per cent), ahead of Paul Reale with 2,384 (39.7 per cent) and Peter Bordignon with 1,159 (19.3 per cent).
claims.episode_span: Marni Moreau won with 2,469 votes, or 41.1 per cent
claims.source_title: The Blue Mountains election results: Marni Moreau elected mayor
claims.supporting_quote: Moreau won with 2,469 votes (41.1 per cent), beating Paul Reale (2,384 voted and 39.7 per cent) and Peter Bordignon (1,159 votes and 19.3 per cent).

claims.claim: Of 15,154 eligible electors in The Blue Mountains, 6,147 voted, a turnout of 40.6 per cent, and the results are unofficial until the clerk certifies them.
claims.episode_span: 6,147 of 15,154 eligible electors voted, a turnout of 40.6 per cent
claims.source_title: The Blue Mountains election results: Marni Moreau elected mayor
claims.supporting_quote: Of the 15,154 eligible electors in The Blue Mountains, 6,147 voted for a turnout of 40.6 per cent.

claims.claim: Gather in Grey won the TIAO Tourism Marketing Campaign Award in the over-$50,000 category in Ottawa on October 23, 2026.

claims.source_title: Grey County marketing campaign wins provincial award
claims.supporting_quote: Gather in Grey recently received the Tourism Industry Association of Ontario (TIAO) Tourism Marketing Campaign Award (Over $50,000 category). The award was presented at the 2026 Ontario Tourism Awards of Excellence in Ottawa on Oct. 23, 2026.

claims.claim: Since the 2025 launch, CollingwoodToday reported more than 50,000 trip idea views and 54,000 event page views, while The Owen Sound Current reported 1.78 million impressions, more than 137,000 YouTube views and more than 315,000 website sessions.
claims.episode_span: more than 50,000 trip idea views and 54,000 event page views
claims.source_title: Grey County’s Gather in Grey Campaign Wins Provincial Tourism Marketing Award
claims.supporting_quote: Since the campaign’s full launch in 2025, the county says it has generated 1.78 million impressions, more than 137,000 YouTube views and more than 315,000 website sessions.

claims.claim: Savanna Myers said the award reflects tourism operators, businesses, artists, farmers, makers, community partners and residents.

claims.source_title: Grey County marketing campaign wins provincial award
claims.supporting_quote: “This recognition reflects the collaborative efforts of tourism operators, businesses, artists, farmers, makers, community partners, and residents whose stories continue to shape Grey County's tourism experience and reputation as a destination where people come together,” said Savanna Myers, Director of Economic Development, Tourism and Culture.
